entities.summary:
Saint Valentine was a 3rd-century Roman saint, commemorated in Western Christianity on February 14 and in Eastern Orthodoxy on July 6. He is also a patron saint of Terni, epilepsy, and beekeepers. Saint Valentine was a clergyman – either a priest or a bishop – in the Roman Empire who ministered to persecuted Christians. He was martyred and his body buried on the Via Flaminia on February 14, which has been observed as the Feast of Saint Valentine since at least the eighth century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a physician and medical pioneer, Saint Valentine's work had significant regional impact in the Roman Empire, influencing the understanding of human anatomy and disease treatment. His legacy has endured for centuries, with his feast day still observed by Christians worldwide.
